question: Create a Manhattan plot from GWAS summary statistics. Plot -log10(p-value) against genomic position, grouped by chromosome. Highlight genome-wide significant SNPs (p < 5x10^-8) in red.

files.eval_guideline: Manhattan plot must show -log10(p-value) vs chromosomal position with SNPs grouped by chromosome and a genome-wide significance threshold (p < 5e-8) visually marked; chromosome colors, significance-SNP marking style, and font may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Both files have the identical filename manhattan_plot.png and PNG image format, directly corresponding to the requested Manhattan plot from GWAS summary statistics.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires visual correctness of the Manhattan plot: -log10(p-value) versus genomic position, chromosome grouping, and a visually marked significance threshold of p < 5e-8. Semantic comparison accommodates the explicitly allowed differences in colors, SNP marking style, and fonts.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images show Manhattan plots of GWAS summary statistics, with genomic position grouped by chromosomes 1–22 on the horizontal axis and −log10(p-value) on the vertical axis. They display matching major association peaks on chromosomes 1, 2, 6, 9, 14, and 16, reaching approximately 11–11.6, along with similar background distributions and isolated weaker signals. Both highlight genome-wide significant SNPs in red and mark the p = 5×10^-8 threshold at approximately 7.3. Both also show a suggestive threshold at −log10(p) = 5. The candidate uses gray and muted blue chromosome colors, dashed or dotted threshold lines, and labels every chromosome; the reference uses black and cyan, solid threshold lines, and omits some chromosome labels. The candidate additionally reports 19,998 SNPs and 199 significant SNPs in its title and legend, counts that cannot be independently verified from the reference alone. These presentation differences do not materially change the scientific interpretation, and no critical required element is missing.
